title: Remove Accents: how it works, formula and examples

content:
The [Remove Accents](/remove-accents) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Strip accents and diacritics — café becomes cafe, résumé becomes resume. Enter your text with accents and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Remove accents and diacritics from text: café becomes cafe, résumé becomes resume, naïve becomes naive. It handles the common Latin accents — acute, grave, circumflex, tilde, umlaut and cedilla — plus special letters such as ø, æ, œ, ł and ß, which are replaced with their closest plain equivalents. The result is plain ASCII-friendly text for file names, URLs, database fields and systems that cannot handle accented characters. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Remove Accents

Start by typing or pasting your text with accents. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Paste or type the text with accents.
2. Read the version without accents — the headline result.
3. Check how many characters were changed, then copy the result.

## How it works

The [Remove Accents](/remove-accents) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. “Café résumé naïve façade — São Paulo, Zürich, Łódź” becomes “Cafe resume naive facade — Sao Paulo, Zurich, Lodz”. Try the same figures in the [Remove Accents](/remove-accents) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Text with accents: Café résumé naïve façade — São Paulo, Zürich, Łódź.), the [Remove Accents](/remove-accents) returns Without accents: Cafe resume naive facade — Sao Paulo, Zurich, Lodz., Characters changed: 10, Original length: 51. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Word Counter](/word-counter) is worth a look before you finish.

## How it works

Accented letters in Unicode are often a base letter plus a combining mark (é is e + ´). Splitting them apart (Unicode normalisation form NFD) and dropping the marks leaves the plain letter. A few letters have no decomposed form — ł, ø, æ, œ and ß — so they are replaced directly: ł becomes l, ø becomes o, æ becomes ae, œ becomes oe and ß becomes ss.

## When you need plain text

Accents break things in surprising places: file names on old systems, URLs, email addresses, database columns with the wrong collation, and search indexes that treat 'resume' and 'résumé' as different words. Stripping accents is also the standard first step in text search and matching — compare the stripped versions and 'Zürich' matches 'Zurich'.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- For URLs, remove accents first, then replace spaces with hyphens and lowercase everything.
- The meaning of a word can change without its accent (résumé vs resume), so check the result before publishing.
- For search, compare accent-stripped versions of both the query and the text.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is a diacritic?

A mark added to a letter that changes its sound — the acute accent in café, the tilde in São, the umlaut in Zürich. This tool removes those marks and leaves the plain base letter. Try it with your own numbers in the [Remove Accents](/remove-accents) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Does it work for non-Latin scripts?

No — it handles Latin-based alphabets (French, Spanish, German, Polish, Portuguese and similar). Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic and Asian scripts are left unchanged. Try it with your own numbers in the [Remove Accents](/remove-accents) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What happens to ß, ø and æ?

They have no plain-letter decomposition, so they are replaced with their closest equivalents: ß becomes ss, ø becomes o, and æ becomes ae. Try it with your own numbers in the [Remove Accents](/remove-accents) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What do I need to use the Remove Accents?

Just Text with accents. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
